exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Automated Collection
exploitedBy.relevance: Unclassified or misclassified PII fields can be automatically harvested by adversaries who exploit the lack of data classification controls to collect sensitive information at scale.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Data from Cloud Storage
exploitedBy.relevance: Misclassified PII fields stored in cloud environments are at risk of unauthorized access and exfiltration from cloud storage due to inadequate classification and protection.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Data from Information Repositories
exploitedBy.relevance: Data retained beyond policy remains in repositories longer than necessary, increasing the window of opportunity for adversaries to access and exfiltrate it.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Data Destruction
exploitedBy.relevance: Excessive retention beyond policy relates directly to failures in data lifecycle management, where required deletion or destruction of data is not performed.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Data Staged
exploitedBy.relevance: Unmasked PII copied into non-production environments effectively stages real sensitive data in less-protected locations, mimicking adversarial data staging behavior.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Unsecured Credentials
exploitedBy.relevance: Insufficient field-level encryption leaves sensitive attributes exposed in a manner analogous to unsecured credentials, making them accessible to adversaries without decryption effort.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Private Keys
exploitedBy.relevance: Lack of field-level encryption for sensitive attributes may expose cryptographic keys or sensitive data that adversaries can leverage directly without needing to crack encryption.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Valid Accounts
exploitedBy.relevance: Overly broad data access means valid account holders can access far more data than their role requires, enabling insider threats or compromised accounts to exfiltrate sensitive information.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Temporary Elevated Cloud Access
exploitedBy.relevance: Excessive access permissions without need-to-know controls mirror the risk of temporary elevated cloud access, where accounts gain more privilege than necessary.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Transfer Data to Cloud Account
exploitedBy.relevance: Cross-border data transfers without adequacy controls directly relate to unauthorized or uncontrolled transfer of data to cloud accounts in foreign jurisdictions.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Lifecycle-Triggered Deletion
exploitedBy.relevance: Insecure or incomplete data disposal directly relates to failures in lifecycle-triggered deletion processes that should ensure data is properly removed.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Disk Content Wipe
exploitedBy.relevance: Incomplete data disposal may leave residual data on storage media that should have been wiped, making disk content wipe techniques relevant to assessing disposal gaps.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: File Deletion
exploitedBy.relevance: Insecure disposal that relies on simple file deletion without secure erasure leaves data recoverable, directly tied to the risks of incomplete file deletion practices.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Business Relationships
exploitedBy.relevance: Absence of audit trails for data lineage obscures how data flows across business relationships and third parties, enabling undetected data misuse or exfiltration.
